latin: Sicut congregatio aquarum est iustus, ita mare ad quod tendunt omnia flumina est diuinitas.
translation: Just as the gathering of the waters is 'the just one,' so the sea to which all the rivers run is 'divinity.'
translation_note: 'congregatio aquarum'/'iustus' ('gathering of waters'/'the just') is, per Farmer, a symbol and alternate name of the ninth sefirah, drawing on Prov. 10:25; 'mare ad quod tendunt omnia flumina'/'diuinitas' ('sea to which all rivers run'/'divinity') symbolizes the Shekhinah, the tenth sefirah, drawing on Eccl. 1:7 (farmer1998:18145).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch11, from Latin at farmer1998:18074

sources.pico_relation: given by Wirszubski as the source passage for the thesis

doctrine: Farmer glosses 'gathering of the waters' (Prov. 10:25) / 'the just' as a symbol and alternate name of the ninth sefirah, and 'sea to which all rivers run' (Eccl. 1:7) / 'divinity' as the Shekhinah, alternate name of the tenth sefirah, directing the reader to the Recanati text quoted by Wirszubski (1989: 42). He compares the thesis's method -- correlating isolated texts of Hebrew Scripture -- to Pico's theses from Proclus (e.g. 24.8), which correlate isolated texts of the Platonic corpus, the aim in both cases being to demonstrate secret harmonies within the respective sacred texts (farmer1998:18145).
context: Farmer cross-references 24.8, on the correspondence in Plato's Phaedrus, Parmenides between 'the back of heaven,' 'the one,' and 'the depth/axis of heaven' (farmer1998:15972); 28.8, on souls descending from the third light to the fourth and fifth days (farmer1998:17645); and 6.7, on how a superior angel illuminates an inferior one (farmer1998:12693) (farmer1998:18145).
historiography: Wirszubski transcribes the thesis as his 'Conclusio XXVII' and gives Recanati, fol. 9va, as its source (wirszubski1989:2404); elsewhere he glosses the underlying scriptural allusion (Eccl. 1:7), explaining that 'all the torrents tend to the sea' because the six extremities called 'torrents' tend, through Tiferet, toward Atheret (the Diadem, the tenth sefirah), which is called 'sea' (wirszubski1989:1705). An unsigned German-language study of Pico's Kabbalistic paradigm (author not established from the material consulted) likewise quotes the thesis in full alongside 5>32, on the Epinomis and the Cabalists' 'world to come' (kabbalah_paradigma:1815).
